title: Numbers 4:34–49
context: Numbers 4:34–49 reports the results of the census of working Levites aged thirty to fifty: Kohathites 2,750, Gershonites 2,630, and Merarites 3,200, for a total of 8,580. A refrain repeats that each was counted ‘according to the commandment of the LORD by Moses’, each ‘according to his service and according to his burden’. Both traditions read the passage as a record of careful obedience, in which God knows and appoints each servant to his work.

verses.text: Moses and Aaron and the princes of the congregation counted the sons of the Kohathites by their families, and by their fathers’ houses,
verses.arminianNotes: Moses, Aaron, and the congregation’s leaders count the Kohathites. Arminians see shared leadership in carrying out God’s command.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree. Both traditions agree on the verse. The princes’ involvement shows that the whole congregation’s leadership took part in obeying God’s instructions.

verses.text: from thirty years old and upward even to fifty years old, everyone who entered into the service for work in the Tent of Meeting.
verses.arminianNotes: Those from thirty to fifty who entered service are counted. Arminians note the faithful application of the standard. The report follows the command of verses 2–3 closely.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed interpreters agree. Both traditions agree on the verse. The wording echoes verse 3, so the fulfillment matches the command.

verses.text: Those who were counted of them by their families were two thousand seven hundred fifty.
verses.arminianNotes: The Kohathites number 2,750. Arminians note this as the record of God’s workers. The Kohathites who carried the most holy things were a relatively small working group.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree. Both traditions note that this contributes to the total in verse 48 and agree on the verse. The census thus records those ready for the most sensitive tabernacle service.

verses.text: These are those who were counted of the families of the Kohathites, all who served in the Tent of Meeting, whom Moses and Aaron counted according to the commandment of the LORD by Moses.
verses.arminianNotes: They were counted ‘according to the commandment of the LORD by Moses’. Arminians see obedience emphasized again. The phrase ‘by Moses’ marks Moses as God’s mediator for the instruction.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed interpreters agree. Both traditions read the refrain as stressing faithful obedience and agree on it. The refrain echoes the obedience language that closes Exodus’s tabernacle account.

verses.text: Those who were counted of the sons of Gershon, by their families, and by their fathers’ houses,
verses.arminianNotes: The Gershonites are counted by families and fathers’ houses. Arminians see the same careful process. The report of the Gershonite census follows the same pattern as the Kohathite report.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree. Both traditions agree on the verse. The parallel structure of verses 34–45 highlights consistent obedience across the clans.

verses.text: from thirty years old and upward even to fifty years old—everyone who entered into the service for work in the Tent of Meeting,
verses.arminianNotes: Those from thirty to fifty who entered service are counted. Arminians note the consistent standard. The same age range applies across all three working clans.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed interpreters agree. Both traditions agree on the verse. The repeated wording keeps the reports in step with the original command.

verses.text: even those who were counted of them, by their families, by their fathers’ houses, were two thousand six hundred thirty.
verses.arminianNotes: The Gershonites number 2,630. Arminians note the record of faithful workers. The Gershonites who carried the fabrics numbered slightly fewer than the Kohathites.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree. Both traditions note this total in relation to verse 48 and agree on the verse. The figure is recorded plainly, without commentary.

verses.text: These are those who were counted of the families of the sons of Gershon, all who served in the Tent of Meeting, whom Moses and Aaron counted according to the commandment of the LORD.
verses.arminianNotes: These Gershonites were counted by Moses and Aaron at the LORD’s command. Arminians see obedience completing each step. Each clan report closes the same way, emphasizing that the count followed God’s word.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed interpreters agree. Both traditions read the refrain as stressing obedience and agree on it. The repeated phrasing shows that Moses and Aaron carried out every part of the command.

verses.text: Those who were counted of the families of the sons of Merari, by their families, by their fathers’ houses,
verses.arminianNotes: The Merarites are counted by families and fathers’ houses. Arminians see the same careful process. The Merarite report completes the three-part pattern of verses 34–45.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree. Both traditions agree on the verse. The parallel structure underscores the uniform obedience of the census.

verses.text: from thirty years old and upward even to fifty years old—everyone who entered into the service for work in the Tent of Meeting,
verses.arminianNotes: Those from thirty to fifty who entered service are counted. Arminians note the consistent standard. The same age range is applied once more.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed interpreters agree. Both traditions agree on the verse. The repetition is characteristic of priestly records that stress exact compliance.

verses.text: even those who were counted of them by their families, were three thousand two hundred.
verses.arminianNotes: The Merarites number 3,200. Arminians note the largest working group carried the heaviest loads. This reflects the Merarites’ responsibility for the heaviest structural pieces.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note the same observation, offered as a reasonable inference rather than a stated reason. Both traditions agree on the verse.

verses.text: These are those who were counted of the families of the sons of Merari, whom Moses and Aaron counted according to the commandment of the LORD by Moses.
verses.arminianNotes: These Merarites were counted at the LORD’s command by Moses. Arminians see obedience emphasized again. The closing formula is the same as for the other clans.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed interpreters agree. Both traditions read the refrain as stressing obedience and agree on it. The final words, ‘by Moses’, again mark Moses as the channel of God’s instruction.

verses.text: All those who were counted of the Levites whom Moses and Aaron and the princes of Israel counted, by their families and by their fathers’ houses,
verses.arminianNotes: All the Levites counted by Moses, Aaron, and the leaders by families and houses. Arminians see a complete and orderly accounting.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree. Both traditions agree on the verse. The summary brings together all three clan reports into one total.

verses.text: from thirty years old and upward even to fifty years old, everyone who entered in to do the work of service and the work of bearing burdens in the Tent of Meeting,
verses.arminianNotes: Those from thirty to fifty doing service and carrying burdens. Arminians see work and burden-bearing honored together. The summary repeats both the age range and the type of service.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed interpreters agree. Both traditions agree on the verse. The double description, work and burden-bearing, sums up the Levites’ role.

verses.text: even those who were counted of them, were eight thousand five hundred eighty.
verses.arminianNotes: The total is 8,580, which matches the clan figures (2,750 + 2,630 + 3,200). Arminians note the exact accounting. This total represents the Levites’ working force, distinct from the 22,000 counted from one month old in chapter 3.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree. Both traditions note that, unlike 3:39, this total matches its parts, and they agree on the verse.

verses.text: According to the commandment of the LORD they were counted by Moses, everyone according to his service and according to his burden. Thus they were counted by him, as the LORD commanded Moses.
verses.arminianNotes: Each was counted ‘according to his service and according to his burden’, as the LORD commanded. Arminians see God appointing each person to a specific task, a dignity for every servant.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed interpreters agree that God assigns each servant his work. Both traditions connect this with the varied gifts and callings in Christ’s body (Romans 12:4–8) and agree on the verse.
